key_insight: A nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic model connects metallic-glass yielding and flow to relaxation dynamics measured independently in stress-relaxation tests.
engineering_relevance: The model supports prediction of temperature- and strain-rate-dependent elastic response, stress overshoot, post-yield softening, and steady flow in metallic glasses.
method: Combine a nonlinear elastic spring with a stretched-exponential dashpot in a Maxwell-type element.
Determine reference material time X₀(ε) from stress relaxation and nonlinear material time X(ε) from elastic–viscoplastic strain decomposition.
Use the Eyring-type ratio φ(ε) = X(ε)/X₀(ε) to quantify deformation-induced changes in relaxation dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports independent stress-relaxation measurements and stress–strain responses as inputs, but provides no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Implementation requires separate relaxation measurements; predictive accuracy beyond the studied conditions is not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic model for the stress-strain and stress-relaxation in metallic glass
